paragraph: No stage is set. No open data policy or draft is on record for Angola. A 2025 World Bank survey records no government open data portal. No change has been found in the last twelve months. A portal with no policy behind it would not count towards Preparing. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying Angola has no open data policy and none is being written.

In December 2022 a World Bank open data readiness assessment found that Benin's [draft access to information bill and its Open Data decree](<https://opendatatoolkit.worldbank.org/content/dam/sites/data/odk/documents/odra-benin.pdf>) were under discussion in government. It saw little progress in over 12 months. From January 2022 to September 2024, [Expertise France ran a technical assistance project](<https://www.expertisefrance.fr/fr/projets/benin-open-data>) supporting the national agency ASSI. Its first axis was an open data regulation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need the government to adopt the policy, and the policy not to have run out.

Botswana has a national Open Data Policy in draft. [Terms of reference issued in March 2026 for open data hackathons funded by the European Union](<https://haus.fi/en/topical/terms-of-reference-support-for-open-data-hackathons-and-forum-in-botswana-phase-2/>) refer to the policy's expected adoption by Parliament. No change has been found in the last twelve months: no source says the policy has been approved or launched, gives the date it was written or names the ministry that wrote it. No government open data portal has been found. Establishing would need the government to adopt the policy, and the policy not to have run out.

Egypt's [National Council for Artificial Intelligence, chaired by the communications minister, adopted the Open Data Policy](<https://techafricanews.com/2025/09/08/egypt-adopts-first-national-open-data-policy-to-drive-digital-transformation/>). It took effect in August 2025 as a transitional framework until a data governance law is passed. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: [in December 2025 the minister listed its launch among the policies Egypt has adopted for digital transformation](<https://gate.ahram.org.eg/News/5356100.aspx>). No source found says a government open data portal has opened under it. Operating would need a government open data portal running under the policy.

[The national portal data.gov.et opened in March 2016, and by June 2018 the ministry and the Central Statistics Agency had posted 29 datasets on it](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/557611531038811117/txt/Disclosable-Version-of-the-ISR-Ethiopia-Supporting-Open-Data-Initiative-P156400-Sequence-No-03.txt>). In the last twelve months Libya's General Information Authority [presented a draft national policy for open government data on 27 November 2025](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2025/11/27/the-general-authority-for-information-launches-the-open-government-data-platform/>), with a technical guide. It said both would go to government bodies for adoption. [On 14 October 2026 it met ministries and sectoral information centres](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/2026/10/15/%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%87%d9%8a%d8%a6%d8%a9-%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%b9%d8%a7%d9%85%d8%a9-%d9%84%d9%84%d9%85%d8%b9%d9%84%d9%88%d9%85%d8%a7%d8%aa-%d8%aa%d8%a8%d8%ad%d8%ab-%d9%85%d8%b9-%d9%85%d9%85%d8%ab%d9%84%d9%8a/>) to finish the final draft of a National Policy for Open Data and Artificial Intelligence. [By February 2026 the authority's Open Government Data Platform held 91 datasets from nine government bodies](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2026/02/11/includes-91-datasets-the-general-authority-for-information-launches-new-indicators-through-the-open-data-platform/>). Its number and approval date are left blank. Its open data section would require every ministry, agency and state company to release non-sensitive datasets. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no source found says the draft has been approved or names a government open data portal. Mauritania's digital transformation ministry dated its [national strategy for open and interoperable data to June 2023](<https://mtnima.gov.mr/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Strategie-de-donnees.pdf>), which makes public bodies' data open by default. On 29 May 2025 the minister [told the National Assembly that the open data and interoperability strategies had been adopted](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/272230>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. In 2025 the government [told the World Bank's GovTech survey that it had no open data portal](<https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037889/govtech-dataset>). Operating would need a government open data portal running under the strategy.

The Ministry of Technology, Communication and Innovation [issued the National Open Data Policy in May 2017](<https://bot.govmu.org/Documents/Strategies/Mauritius%20Open%20Data%20Policy%20May%202017.pdf>). It makes public datasets open by default and has no end date. The government [told the World Bank's GovTech survey in 2025 that data.govmu.org is its open data portal](<https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0037889/govtech-dataset>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from the last three years names a ministry that has released data on the portal, or counts its datasets. Mature would need a source naming a ministry or agency that has released data under the policy, or counting the datasets or the bodies publishing.

A [CSEA policy brief of November 2025](<https://cpanel.cseaafrica.org/images/posts/62181895.pdf>) finds that Malawi's open data vision is spread across other instruments. It finds no dedicated open data implementation framework and no central authority to enforce open standards. [On 3 September 2025 the OGP Malawi Secretariat announced](<https://ogp.gov.mw/events/malawi-launches-new-open-data-portal>) that Malawi had launched a new Open Data Portal under its Third National Action Plan. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names the ministries or agencies that publish on the portal, or counts its datasets. Preparing would need an open data policy, strategy, decree or law being written or out for consultation.

The Federal Ministry of Communications [issued the Nigeria Open Data Policy in July 2018](<https://nipc.gov.ng/assets/resources/nigeria-open-data-policy/nigeria-open-data-policy.pdf>). It applies to every federal ministry, department and agency and requires them to release their data open by default. The policy says Data.gov.ng has been built as the national catalogue of open data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found from the last three years names an agency that has released data on the catalogue, or counts its datasets. Mature would need a source naming a ministry or agency that has released data under the policy, or counting the datasets or the bodies publishing.

Rwanda's [National Data Sharing Policy for the public sector was reported in place in May 2026](<https://cenfri.org/articles/what-will-determine-the-success-of-rwandas-data-governance-push/>). It makes government data open by default, subject to classification and access controls. The rule on open data is part of that policy, and no separate open data policy is on record. No earlier position has been found, so no change is recorded in the last twelve months. No source found names a government open data portal running under the policy. Operating would need such a portal running under the policy.

Tunisia's [government decree 2021-3 of 6 January 2021 organises the publication of public data on the principle that it is open by default](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/decret-gouvernemental-n-2021-3-du-6-janvier-2021-relatif-aux-donnees-publiques-ouvertes/>). [A new version of the national open data portal, built to the decree's specifications, opened in early March 2023](<https://www.opengovpartnership.org/fr/members/tunisia/commitments/TN0053/>), and [in April 2024 it carried datasets from 23 data producers across six themes](<https://www.opengovpartnership.org/fr/members/tunisia/commitments/TN0053/>). In the last twelve months, [a national strategy for governing, opening and using public data was presented in final draft on 26 March 2026](<http://www.ogptunisie.gov.tn/?p=6651>). It [still awaited the government's endorsement in August 2026](<https://www.opengovpartnership.org/documents/tunisia-results-report-2023-2025/>). No source found reports the strategy to have been adopted.

The World Bank's [SOGDAT year 3 report](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/933101529919350715/txt/SOGDAT-Year-3-Report.txt>), covering February 2016 to June 2017, says Tanzania's Open Data Task Force drafted the National Open Data Policy in 2016. It went to the Ministry of Finance for submission to Cabinet in December 2016, and by June 2017 it had not been officially adopted. The portal opendata.go.tz, launched in September 2015, then held 163 datasets from 11 institutions. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether the policy was adopted after June 2017. Establishing would need the government to adopt the policy, and the policy not to have run out.

The Ministry of ICT and National Guidance [reported for the year to June 2022 that a draft Open Data Policy had been circulated to its staff](<https://budget.finance.go.ug/sites/default/files/Sector%20Spending%20Agency%20Budgets%20and%20Performance/2021-2022_QuarterlyReport_Q4_020_MinistryofICTandNationalGuidance_05082022195509.pdf>). The same report says work continued on getting an open data portal running. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No later source found says the draft has gone to cabinet or been adopted, or that the portal has opened to the public. Establishing would need the government to adopt the policy, and the policy not to have run out.

[Research ICT Africa says it developed an Open Data Policy Framework for South Africa](<https://researchictafrica.net/project/datacipation-shaping-harmonised-and-inclusive-digital-and-data-policies-in-africa/>) in 2026, in a project with GIZ and AUDA-NEPAD. Its project page, from September 2026, does not say who commissioned the framework or whether the government has approved it. The framework dates from the last twelve months, and no source found says the government has adopted it. No national open data portal has been found, and no data published under an open data policy. Establishing would need an open data policy adopted and still running.
